newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle seen priced $68-$69 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle seen priced $68-$69 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Monday were seen priced $68.00 to $69.00 by owners anticipating a rebound in beef prices, feedlot sources said.
Several feedlot managers said the market was anticipating stronger beef prices following recent steep declines, which should make beef attractive to retailers, they said.
Beef prices have declined steadily since March 25, with heavier-weight choice beef losing $4.05 per cwt from that period to its midday quote of $100.16, USDA statistics showed.
Fed cattle prices also were seen underpinned by ideas packers were short-bought on live cattle supplies, they said.

If packers are short-bought and beef prices rally as expected, this could offset potential weakness from a carryover of unsold cattle from this week's showlists, the sources said. The bulk of this week's cattle sold Wednesday at $67.00. There were light sales at $66.00 Thursday and Friday.
About 2,000 head sold in the Panhandle on Friday and about 200 in Kansas.
But volume in the Panhandle and Kansas was too light for an adequate test and light sales in Kansas were for cattle that were below the same quality that sold Wednesday, the feedlot sources said.
